page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 33 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 and AES instruction sets. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.se1.2xlarge delivers modest compute performance. Single-core and multi-core CPU benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, consistently place the instance in the bottom 25 percent of tested hardware. Single-threaded compression and decompression performance is also limited, falling into the bottom 10 percent. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in large-block memory bandwidth read and write operations, as well as in Passmark CPU tests and Redis SET operations. Large-model LLM inference is highly constrained, though small-model inference speeds remain average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1.2xlarge offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU processing. The lack of local storage and moderate network bandwidth are key architectural tradeoffs to consider. This instance is best suited for workloads such as medium-sized databases, caching layers like Redis, memory-intensive data processing, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring a larger memory footprint without high-frequency compute demands.
